;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in Sri Lanka]]
**Gunmen open fire on two buses carrying [[Islam in Sri Lanka|Muslim]] voters to the [[2019 Sri Lankan presidential election|polls]] near [[Anuradhapura]]. No casualties are reported and no arrests take place. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/16/sri-lanka-presidential-election-gunmen-fire-on-buses-carrying-muslim-voters (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**Turkey blames [[November 2019 Syria bombings|another attack]] on the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party|PKK]]. The bombings targeted a bus terminal in [[al-Bab]], [[Aleppo Governorate]], killing 18 and wounding dozens of others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/deadly-car-bomb-blasts-rip-bus-terminal-syria-al-bab-191116111934634.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 Iraqi protests]]
**A [[car bomb]] detonates near a protest in [[Baghdad]], killing two people and injuring 20. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security-blast/baghdad-bomb-kills-two-injures-12-security-sources-idUSKBN1XP280 (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/deadly-bomb-explosion-hits-baghdad-anti-gov-protests-191116060825739.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Gaza–Israel clashes (November 2019)]]
**Continuing [[Palestinian rocket attacks on Israel|rocket fire]] leads [[Israel]] to launch fresh strikes into [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] in response. [https://www.france24.com/en/20191116-israel-launches-fresh-strikes-against-gaza-after-rocket-fire (France 24)]
*An attack on civilians in the village of Mbau, [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], using bladed weapons, kills over 18 civilians. Islamic militants are the suspected attackers. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/at-least-15-civilians-killed-in-eastern-congo-by-suspected-islamist-militants-idUSKBN1XQ0IM?il=0 (Reuters)] 
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**At least eight people were killed and dozens injured in [[Sacaba]] after security forces fired on supporters of ousted president [[Evo Morales]]. [https://www.npr.org/2019/11/16/780118421/8-killed-in-bolivia-as-protesters-call-for-return-of-ousted-president-evo-morale (NPR)] [https://apnews.com/530280a8d9674f58ad19af8d3f00edee (Associated Press)]
**Bolivia's interim president met with a UN envoy, Jean Arnault, to discuss the country's political turmoil. [https://globalnews.ca/news/6179230/bolivia-united-nations-unrest/ (Global News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[LGBT rights in Hong Kong]]
**Amid violent protests, [[Hong Kong]] holds its [[gay pride parade]] in spite of a police ban. Human rights and pro-democracy and [[openly gay]] activist [[Jimmy Sham]] heads the march. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/asia/hong-kong-s-pride-parade-marches-on-despite-city-wide-protests-20191116-p53b9t.html (''The Sydney Morning Herald'')]

;International relations 
*[[Iran–United States relations]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Egypt–Iran relations]], [[Iran–United Arab Emirates relations]], [[Bahrain–Iran relations]], [[Shia–Sunni relations]]
**[[United States Air Force Chief of Staff]] [[David Goldfein]] asks [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf States]] to be united amid rising tensions with Iran as [[Saudi Arabia]], the [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]], [[Bahrain]] and [[Egypt]] have [[Qatar–Saudi Arabia diplomatic conflict|divided]] opinions with [[Qatar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-emirates-airshow-gulf-security/u-s-air-force-chief-of-staff-calls-for-gulf-arab-unity-to-counter-iran-idUSKBN1XQ095 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2019]]
**A man killed his estranged wife and their three children and injured another child before killing himself in [[San Diego]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/16/us/san-diego-shooting.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–2020 Iranian protests|2019 Iranian fuel protests]] 
**Large protests rock major Iranian cities with clashes reported between protesters and security forces. [https://en.radiofarda.com/a/as-protests-spread-in-iran-clashes-reported-with-security-forces/30275112.html (Radio Farda)]
*[[2019 Sri Lankan presidential election]]
**[[Sri Lanka]]n voters head to the polls to elect a new [[President of Sri Lanka|president]]. Although 35 candidates are running, the main frontrunners are former [[Minister of Defence (Sri Lanka)|Defense Secretary]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] of the right-wing [[Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna|Sri Lanka People's Front]] and current [[Ministry of Housing and Construction (Sri Lanka)|Minister of Housing and Construction]] [[Sajith Premadasa]] of the centre-right [[United National Party]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sri-lanka-election/polls-close-in-sri-lanka-presidential-poll-marred-by-violence-idUSKBN1XQ059?il=0 (Reuters)]
**Rajapaksa claims victory and Premadasa concedes defeat, with half of the votes counted for. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sri-lanka-election/sri-lanka-strongman-rajapaksa-set-to-become-president-after-rival-concedes-defeat-idUSKBN1XR023?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Yellow vests movement]]
**[[Paris|Parisian]] [[Paris Police Prefecture|police]] fire [[tear gas]] and [[water cannon]]s at protestors and arrest around 105 people on the anniversary of the first yellow vest protests. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-protests-anniversary/paris-police-use-tear-gas-water-cannon-on-yellow-vest-protests-anniversary-idUSKBN1XQ0BN (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Louisiana gubernatorial election]]
**Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[John Bel Edwards]] narrowly defeats businessman and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] candidate [[Eddie Rispone]] to retain his seat; Louisiana Republicans also fall short of winning a supermajority in the [[Louisiana House of Representatives]], allowing Edwards to retain veto power over legislation. The results follow recent gains by the Democratic Party in elections in [[2019 Virginia elections|Virginia]] and [[2019 Kentucky gubernatorial election|Kentucky]] and is considered as another blow to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-louisiana-results/louisianas-democratic-governor-wins-re-election-in-republican-leaning-state-media-idUSKBN1XR05E?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2020 Hong Kong protests]]
**In [[Hong Kong]], soldiers belonging to [[China]]'s [[People's Liberation Army]] are spotted in the streets helping clear debris left by protesters. [https://www.theepochtimes.com/chinese-soldiers-make-first-appearance-amid-hong-kong-protests-clear-debris-from-street_3148309.html (''The Epoch Times'')]
*[[Milion chvilek pro demokracii|Protests in the Czech Republic]]
**On the 30th anniversary of the outbreak of the [[Velvet Revolution]], over 200,000 people gathered at [[Letná|Letná, Prague]], demanding better political culture and the resignation of prime minister [[Andrej Babiš]]. This was the second mass demonstration organized at Letná by [[Milion chvilek pro demokracii]] after [[Je to na nás!|a similar protest on 23 June 2019]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-50446661 (BBC News)]
